cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fair Exchange
cards.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Half an hour helping you move buys two hours painting my shed on Saturday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Saturday's my only lie-in. Can I come after lunch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Afternoon painting costs me cricket. Three hours, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hire a painter. But I need the sofa carried up three flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then two painter-hours covers loading; the stairs cost a third. Cricket's free again.

mechanism: A treats repricing a moving favor as tuition in negotiation and claims credit for the pupil hired-help counteroffer.
confusable: Unlike outdoing favors, A bargains for a compensating return rather than offering more help.
comparison: Pan effort reduction versus timing preference exchanged for hired labor.
seedUse: D46 move/cricket/painter/stairs; S05 correction of how the trainee calculates cost.
